lines.text: OraclePhys: A Systematic Framework for
LLM Fine-Tuning on
Structural Mechanics
Mingyu Li , Guorui Song , Jing Lin , Haoqian Wang
University of Houston, Tsinghua University
Correspondence: mli52@cougarnet.uh.edu
Abstract
What a language model internalizes from fine-
tuning is usually diagnosed after the fact. We
make it an experimental variable. Oracle-
Phys is a systematic fine-tuning framework
with three components: OraclePhys-Bench ,
an exactly-graded structural-mechanics bench-
mark whose finite-element oracle scores ev-
ery answer and counterfactual edit—no hu-
man labels, no LLM judging; OraclePhys-
30K , a supervision dataset of seven answer
forms over byte-identical structure descrip-
tions; and a controlled training study across
the seven forms and three verifier roles. The
study yields two findings. First, the label’s
answer form—not its bit count—causally de-
termines what fine-tuning teaches: a ranking
objective installs an out-of-distribution forward
model where the untrained base sits at the
guessing prior, a scalar objective at best a
partial one, a boolean nothing detectable; the
vector–scalar gulf survives a second physics
domain, a second model family, and a para-
phrased evaluation surface. Second, written
or score-filtered answers install this capability,
while advantage-weighted scores (GRPO) raise
reward yet leave the model statistically equiv-
alent to its start on held-out physics—within
the recipes and budgets tested—sufficing only
for routing. The trained 8B—the first LLM on
spatial structural response—reaches the task’s
data-precision frontier: above a frontier LLM at
zero- and 32-shot, at a specialist’s level. What
the label spells out about the target computa-
tion is what fine-tuning teaches; what you train
on is what you route.
1 Introduction
Training objectives are usually chosen for grade-
ability: a scalar loss, a pass/fail check, a prefer-
ence score. What a language model internalizes
under a given objective is diagnosed only after the
fact, by probing or benchmarking—a literature of
striking negative results (Vafa et al., 2024; Wang
et al., 2024) that observes but does not intervene.
Whether the objective itself causally determines
what is internalized, everything else held fixed, has
not been isolated as an experimental variable.
We isolate it with OraclePhys-Bench (§2): a
finite-element solver returns the exact per-story lat-
eral response of any steel frame; the spatial target is
non-local in the input text, and intervention probes
have verified answers.
The testbed is a model organism for a question
about training, not a benchmark of engineering
practice. Whether the label’s answer form deter-
mines what fine-tuning teaches is live well beyond
this domain (Kung and Peng, 2023; Webson and
Pavlick, 2022; Zhou et al., 2023). Deciding be-
tween such readings requires byte-identical inputs,
labels with controlled information content, and a
grader that scores every counterfactual—properties
no natural corpus offers and this domain provides
by construction (Li et al., 2023). The price—a sin-
gle training template—is stated in Limitations; the
purchase: every contrast is controlled, not correla-
tional.
The experiment trains on OraclePhys-30K ,
holding the base model, training structures, and in-
put text byte-identical and varying only the answer
form the objective demands: full per-story ranking
(P), peak scalar (A), or pass/fail boolean (O). The
ranking objective installs a forward model (0.86–
0.91 OOD localization vs. 0.19–0.25 untrained),
the scalar at best a partial one, the boolean nothing
detectable (§3); the vector–scalar gulf replicates on
a second physics domain, a second model family,
and a paraphrased evaluation surface.
The same oracle then dissociates the ways a ver-
ifier can enter training (§4–5): written or score-
filtered answers install; advantage-weighted scores
leave the model statistically equivalent to its start
while reward climbs—yet suffice to wire a − 0 . 15

Ceiling analyses (§6) locate these results: a fron-

by task difficulty.
Contributions.
• We build OraclePhys-Bench , an exactly-graded
testbed for structural mechanics, with verified
surface-cue removal, intervention probes, and
an isomorphic second domain—a controlled in-
strument, not a leaderboard.
• We release OraclePhys-30K , a supervision
dataset of seven answer forms over byte-
identical structure descriptions.
• We present the first LLM trained on per-story
structural response (prior systems wrap solvers
or treat scalar beam statics; §7), via a controlled
study—seven supervision forms, three verifier
roles, one exact oracle—training an 8B to the
task’s data-precision frontier : above Claude
Opus 4.8 at zero- and 32-shot, at a specialist
GNN’s level.
• We establish two findings : the answer form of
the supervision label, not its bit count, deter-
mines what fine-tuning teaches; and, within the
recipes tested, written or score-filtered answers
teach what advantage-weighted scores do not—
scores suffice for routing, not for installation.
2 An Oracle-Graded Testbed for Spatial
Forward Models
2.1 Task and oracle
The subject domain is the lateral response of 2-
D steel frames (Fig. 1): multi-story, multi-bay,
with per-story sections, a connection type, optional
answer the objective exposes (Eq. 2). Bottom: the four
braces, damage events, and a lateral load whose
vertical profile varies. An OpenSees finite-element
model returns, for any structure, the per-story inter-
story drift ratios

where u k is the lateral displacement of floor k
( u 0 =0 at the base) and h k the story height; the
governing story k is the story that governs the
design. Soft or damaged stories drift more, and
a brace stiffens its story. The FE solution defines
ground truth for this task, and grading against it is
deterministic and exact, so no human annotation
and no model-based judging appear anywhere in
training or evaluation.
The model sees only a natural-language descrip-
tion (geometry, per-story sections, connections,
braces, damage, load) and must rank all stories
by drift, in JSON. Primary metrics: top-1 local-
ization of the governing story and Spearman ρ of
the full ranking, on held-out structures ( n =150 per
axis; 80 for extrapolation).
Two properties make this testbed diagnostic
rather than merely hard: structural weakness is spa-
tially non-local (no single sentence of the descrip-
tion reveals the governing story), and every claimed
capability can be probed by intervention —the or-
acle grades counterfactuals, so “strengthen a story;
where does weakness move?” has a verified an-
swer. Throughout the paper, “installs a forward
model” (our operationalization of a world model in
this domain) is a behavioral claim—performance
on the intervention-probing axes of §2.2—not a
claim about internal representations. Not for lack
of trying: linear probes decode the governing
story equally from every arm— including the be-
haviorally inert O—at a surface-level baseline;
probe-based measurement is insensitive to a two-
to-sixfold behavioral difference here (Limitations).
2.2 Evaluation axes
All axes use deterministic instance streams (§2.4)
and the same parser; a parse failure scores as a
miss.
Forward localization / ranking : rank the sto-
ries of an unseen structure (OOD structures have
5–6 stories vs. 3–4 in training, so every test rank-
ing is longer than any seen in training). Post-
intervention forward : the governing story is
strengthened; localize the new one from the edited
description—anti-correlated with the pre-edit an-
swer by construction (post-edit family present in
training; Limitations). Two-step horizon : two se-
quential edits—errors compound. Extrapolation :
forward localization on the tallest structures. Ac-
tion interface : the original structure plus a one-
sentence action (“add a brace to story 3”), applied
internally; a paired control rewrites the same transi-
tion as a full post-edit description, so the act − desc
gap isolates action-application (§5). Invariance
(sanity): strengthening a story must not make it
relatively weaker.
2.3 Two difficulty tiers, and killing the surface
Tier-1 (realistic) structures follow design practice,
leaving exploitable regularities; tier-2 (hardened)
randomizes them (section jitter, composed weak-
ening, varied load shapes). Hardening is verified :
a bag-of-words probe falls 0 . 63 → 0 . 26 (chance
0.18), the structured-feature probe from 0.76 to
0.57, a geometry-only probe staying near tier-1
(Appendix B)—no lexical shortcut that clears the
first-order formula survives.
The non-learning reference is a 30-line first-
order formula (story shear over a stiffness proxy).
It is biased against us—it reads numeric section
properties directly from the design object—and its
tier-2 scores (0.45/0.47) sit well above random: any
physics claim must clear this row.
2.4 Splits, determinism, and statistics
Training structures have 3–4 stories; the OOD pool
has 5–6 under held-out geometry. All streams gen-
erate deterministically from fixed seeds: every run—
across models, checkpoints, months—answers the
same 150 questions per axis. This buys three things.
(i) Bit-exact reproducibility under greedy decod-
ing and fixed batching. (ii) Paired statistics : per-
instance correctness arrays are stored in every re-
sults file, and all model comparisons are exact Mc-
Nemar tests (McNemar, 1947) on discordant pairs
with paired bootstrap CIs. This paper reports ∼ 50
paired tests; the staircase claims rest on p < 10
effects that survive any standard multiplicity cor-
rection; the answers-vs-scores dissociation rests on
installation effects at p ≤ 0 . 005 and on powered
direct endpoint contrasts on fresh n =600 streams
( n =1800 pooled over disjoint axes, p < 10 ;
Table 8); and we treat p ∈ [0 . 01 , 0 . 05] results
that do not survive the Table 5 FDR as secondary,
corroborating evidence. (iii) Machine-checkable
provenance : one script regenerates every number
from archived per-instance files, pairing fingerprint-
checked; the exported streams, grader, and refer-
ence rows constitute OraclePhys-Bench , and fresh
streams mint on demand as a contamination de-
fense.

3.2 The vector–scalar gulf, three times
Fig. 2 shows OOD governing-story localization
across frames/Qwen (3 seeds), heat/Qwen, and

physics domain—2-D steady-state heat conduction,
a structural isomorph (rows ↔ stories, cooling ↔
braces) with its own surface-cue audit—and on a
second model family with the same data and recipe.
The scalar arm’s partial emergence is the excep-

The gate survives a second linguistic surface.
Re-rendering the held-out instances through a para-
phrased template (running prose, reordered fields,
reworded phrasings; identical information, ques-
tion, and parser) and re-evaluating the frozen check-
points leaves the gate unchanged: raw P 0.847 vs.
its own checkpoint’s 0.887 (3-seed mean 0.86),
and calibrated ladder 0.75/0.44/0.31/0.29 vs. the
original 0.73/0.47/0.33/0.30 (Table 9). What the
ranking objective installs is readable from a surface
it was never trained on; the scalar arm is the more
surface-sensitive (raw 0.35).
3.4 Controls: format, task proximity, bit
count
Does the staircase measure the label’s information,
or merely the proximity between training task and
evaluation? Four further arms, all on byte-identical
structure text, dissociate the candidates. K keeps
A’s scalar format but changes the content: each ex-
ample asks for the drift of one randomly designated
story ( {"story_drift": 0.0041} ), exposing the per-
story field pointwise—never a ranking. V asks for
the full drift-value vector—an information superset
of the ranking, since values determine order. G
asks only which story governs ( ∼ log n s ≈ 2 bits).
S is the placebo: P’s question and answer format
verbatim, with content-free shuffled permutations
as labels—a training-side control task in the sense
of Hewitt and Liang (2019).
The suite orders as: base 0.30 ≈ S 0.35 < A
(calibrated localization; key tests: K > A p =10 ,
ble 5). Three readings. Format installs nothing :
the placebo stays at base (and degrades interven-
tion behavior, − 0 . 06 ); K, which never produced
a ranking, recovers over half the gulf under cali-
bration (raw K = A), bounding task proximity at
+0 . 13 in that regime. (Control-suite arms are sin-
gle runs, read against the gate arms’ seed spread;
see Limitations.) Bit count alone does not explain
it : against the expectation pre-stated in the released
builder, the value vector—an information super-
set of the ranking—lands on the pointwise arm
( p =1 . 0 ) and below P: value content plausibly in-
stalls a magnitude-reading model whose derived
orderings pay the precision toll of §6—a hypothesis
our ordinal probes cannot test; the value-readout
axis (Limitations) would decide it. Supervision
mass fails the same test: the shortest label (G)
lands highest among controls, the longest (V) does
not. Two pincers close on one conclusion—on the
amount axis, minimal G matches P while superset
V does not; on the operation axis (calibrated), value
arms lead A on forward reading while A leads
them post-intervention—each killing one mono-
tone story. The answer itself does : two bits naming
the governing story buy 0.68 localization, not dis-
tinguishable from P at our single-run resolution
( p =0 . 27 ; G trails on full-ranking ρ , 0.72 vs. 0.86).
The content- type dissociation also appears post-
intervention under calibration : V trails A ( − 0 . 107 ,
p =0 . 011 , q =0 . 04 ) despite leading on localization—
scoped to that regime (the raw rows order differ-
ently, and no parse-level data yet separates format
from knowledge there; the main staircase is invari-
ant across both). Across the suite, what installs
tracks what the label spells out—format and bit
count closed, task proximity bounded.

4 One Oracle, Two Uses: Answers Install;
Advantage-Weighted Scores Do Not
Design. The oracle enters training in three roles—
teacher , filter , judge —collapsing into two uses:
answers versus scores. From the same start (the
tier-1 P arm, 0.660 tier-2) on the same hardened
pool, the teacher protocol trains on oracle-written
rankings (dense SFT); the judge optimizes ora-
cle scores of sampled rankings (GRPO; budgets in
Appendix C). Weights, LoRA configuration, and
prompts are shared: the variable is how the oracle’s
knowledge enters the gradient (Fig. 3).

+0 . 14 across axes (Table 1, Appendix D; seed
42; 3 seeds: forward 0 . 731 ± 0 . 011 from 0.660,
post-intervention 0 . 691 ± 0 . 008 , the latter individ-
ually significant in every seed, p ≤ 0 . 0013 ) with
essentially no tier-1 forgetting ( 0 . 887 → 0 . 867 ).
(Convention: paired rows cite the canonical seed-
42 checkpoint, 0.747 forward; seed means are re-
ported wherever 3 seeds exist.) The judge pro-
tocol leaves the forward, extrapolation, and two-
step axes within noise (Tables 5, 6; the one post-
intervention cell is flagged below)— while its own
reward climbs 0.80 to 0.93 : margins sharpen on
already-solved instances, which the reward reg-
isters and accuracy does not. Powered direct
contrasts settle the endpoint comparison: pool-
ing the three disjoint OOD axes on fresh n =600
streams, the dense endpoint leads GRPO round-

Table 8).
Three further cells complete the picture. RL
on the strongest base: GRPO continued from
the dense-SFT checkpoint under a matched oracle-
call budget lands at 0.760 vs. 0.747 ( ∆ = +0 . 01 ,
p = 0 . 81 ): once the knowledge is installed, scores
have nothing detectable left to add. RL from
scratch: GRPO from the untrained base raises

on tier-1—below the formula’s 0.533—and at ran-

(Shao et al., 2025). The one candidate RL instal-

either reading; on the fresh n =600 stream it dis-
solves ( +0 . 017 , p =0 . 35 ): the judge-side null is
uniform at higher power.
Provenance, recipe, and headroom controls.
Filtered self-distillation (the STaR/RAFT/ReST
recipe, used here as a measurement; Zelikman
et al., 2022; Dong et al., 2023; Gulcehre et al.,
2023; Singh et al., 2024 ): sample 50 per hard-
ened prompt from the P checkpoint, oracle- score ,
keep the best with reward ≥ 0 . 9 (93% cover-
age), imitate the survivors—the oracle contributes
nothing but scores, yet the gradient is dense im-
itation. This installs ( +0 . 093 forward, +0 . 127
post-intervention; p ≤ 0 . 005 , Tables 3, 5), indis-
tinguishably from oracle-written labels (one cost:
tier-1 retention 0.820 vs. 0.867). This cell dou-
bles as the pool-adequacy control : the sampled
pool demonstrably contains transferable signal—
a dense update extracts it; group-relative advan-
tages did not. Best-practice GRPO —group size
50, a difficulty-filtered pool, the strongest SFT
base, ∼ 10 × the dense round’s oracle-call budget—
lands at +0 . 033 on its first seed ( p =0 . 18 ); across
three seeds, 0 . 751 ± 0 . 030 against the 0.747 start, a
mean gain of +0 . 004 . Headroom-matched GRPO —
the identical recipe from the pre-hardening 0.660
start, whose runway ( +0 . 12 across the four axes)
the dense round itself consumed—moves +0 . 013
in-pool localization 0 . 41 → 0 . 55 ; Fig. 8). Update-
scale probe: dense SFT trains at ∼ 100 × GRPO’s
learning rate with multi-epoch reuse (budgets in
Appendix C), so we re-ran best-practice GRPO at
tenfold lr ( 10 ): it does not unlock installation
but erodes it (forward 0 . 747 → 0 . 680 ; four-axis
pooled − 0 . 074 , p =8 × 10 , Table 6)—within this
window, the null does not reverse with update mag-
nitude. (In-pool comparisons exist, Xiong et al.,
2025; Chen et al., 2025; ours add the held-out out-
come and an oracle-label control.) The same sam-
pled tail, selected by the same verifier, transferred
under dense imitation and did not under group-
relative advantages; why consolidation transfers
under one update and not the other we leave open
(candidates: token-level credit assignment, multi-
epoch reuse of survivors, the KL-conservatism of
on-policy updates, Shenfeld et al., 2025).
Alternative explanations. Five rival readings—
reward sparsity, optimizer failure, exploration,
headroom, capacity—fail against dedicated cells
(Appendix D); most pointedly, endpoints track
starting points ( 0 . 678 ± 0 . 014 from 0.660, where
oracle labels reach 0.747), and the same LoRA rank
accepts the knowledge whenever the oracle writes
or filters it.

Scope. These are results for one task family, one
algorithm (GRPO), one scale (8B+LoRA), ≤ 800
steps, lr 10 – 10 ; prolonged-RL regimes (Liu
et al., 2025a) are not contradicted. Within this
regime the dissociation is clean—the score’s failure

and adds an oracle-graded controlled cell to the
elicitation-vs-expansion debate (Yue et al., 2025;
Chu et al., 2025).
5 Interfaces Are Cheap, Knowledge Is
Not
An installed model that cannot be addressed.
The dense-SFT model of §4 knows the post-edit
response (0.667/0.680 given the edited description)
but cannot apply an action: handed the original
structure plus “add braces to story 3,” it drops to
0.513/0.533—a − 0 . 15 interface gap on both tiers
(Fig. 7, appendix). Installed, but not wired to the
state + action interface.
Scores suffice to wire it. Action-format GRPO—
prompts are (state, random-story action) pairs, re-
ward is the oracle’s score of the predicted post-
action ranking—closes the gap exactly: tier-2 act
0 . 533 → 0 . 687 vs. desc 0.687 (discordant 15:15,
p =1 . 0 ; Tables 5, 7), tier-1 0.76 vs. 0.73, with
the forward and post-intervention axes at parity.
This matches §4’s decomposition: the interface
task starts half-right, so sampled behavior is rich
in successes for selection to amplify (the transfer
asymmetry of §4 notwithstanding).
But routing is not RL-specific: the dense con-
trol. If wiring only takes training on the interface,
dense supervision should do it too—and it does,
plus more: SFT on the same action distribution (4k
oracle-labeled pairs) closes the gap just as com-
pletely (tier-2 act 0 . 533 → 0 . 760 , p = 6 × 10 ;
own act − desc gap n.s.) at zero knowledge tax
(forward 0.740 vs. 0.747). On tier-1 it beats the
RL route: post-intervention +0 . 140 (discordant
26:5, p = 2 × 10 ), reaching 0.867—the paper’s
highest post-intervention score—with act +0 . 087
( p = 0 . 015 , secondary) trending the same way.
The dissociation, sharpened. Wiring an inter-
face is cheap : either use of the oracle buys it. In-
stalling knowledge is expensive : only dense an-
swers buy it, at any score budget we tested—and
they install additional knowledge while wiring. In
this regime, scores sufficed for routing and for
nothing else we could measure —a narrow role
that dense supervision fills at least as well wher-
ever answers can be demonstrated. (Practically,
pure SFT yields the best all-around model—action-
SFT, post-intervention 0.867; the §6 rows belong
to the assembled final checkpoint.)
The thinking channel: no measurable bene-
fit, a possible cost. Three pre-specified tier-2
contrasts (Appendix E) find no benefit from an
explicit reasoning channel: repairing the chan-
nel that direct-answer SFT breaks costs knowl-
edge ( − 0 . 073 , p =0 . 013 , the only significant ef-
fect), thinking-on buys nothing, and think-RL vs.
matched-compute nothink-RL is a tie favoring not
thinking. Where the bottleneck is missing knowl-
edge, deliberation cannot substitute for installation
(Lightman et al., 2024).
6 Ceilings: Frontier, Specialist, and the
Data-Precision Frontier
The frontier model we test sits near a 30-
line formula. Under a controlled API proto-
col (Appendix C), Claude Opus 4.8 localizes at
0.633/0.500 (tier-1/2). Against the first-order for-
mula of §2.3 its lead is at most +0 . 10 (tier-1
forward, p = 10 ) and +0 . 073 (tier-2 post-
intervention, p = 0 . 013 , secondary), n.s. on the
other two cells—within a hair of thirty lines of
physics, once surface cues are killed.
In-context examples do not install it. The com-
parison is asymmetric—our model saw 4k oracle-
labeled structures, the frontier model none. The in-
context control narrows it: with 32 oracle-labeled
worked examples Opus does not improve (tier-2
0 . 500 → 0 . 433 , p = 0 . 087 ; statistically still at the
formula, p =0 . 86 , Table 6), while the trained 8B ex-
ceeds this 32-shot frontier by +0 . 300 ( p < 10 ;
Fig. 6, appendix). In this design, in-context adapta-
tion did not install what weight updates did (many-
shot and tool use untested; Limitations).
A specialist baseline at parity. A per-story GNN
reading structured graph input —numeric sections,
bracing topology, damage, load shape as features—
trains on the same distribution and evaluates on
the same instance streams. On tier-2 it matches
our final text-reading model (0.733/0.733 forward,
0.680/0.680 post-intervention; discordants in Ta-
ble 5); on fresh streams the pooled difference is
bounded within ± 0 . 06 ( n =1200 , n.s., point esti-
mate toward the LLM; Table 8). On tier-1 the
LLM leads (0.84 vs. 0.82 forward; +0 . 100 post-
int, p = 0 . 058 ). When the testbed gained its load-
shape parameter, the GNN was blind until hand-
rewired; the LLM read the change from a sentence.
The 0.73–0.78 convergence is a data-precision
frontier. Six learners with different inductive bi-
ases (0.733–0.780; Appendix F) converge on the
same tier-2 band with no significant pairwise differ-
ence. The margin structure explains why (Fig. 4):
34% of tier-2 instances have a top-2 drift margin
under 10%, so ± 5% per-story error caps top-1 at
0.83 and ± 8% at 0.78—bracketing the band. The
band is a data-precision frontier , not a task ceiling:
the task is noiseless, and RL’s consolidation moves
within the wall without crossing it.
What moves the frontier—and what does not.
The data-efficiency curve (Fig. 5) locates the
binding constraint: tier-1 saturates by n = 1 k;
tier-2 crawls ( +0 . 02 at the last doubling)—while
one difficulty-matched second round buys +0 . 09 ,
worth three doublings. What is scarce is informa-
tion near the decision boundary—curriculum beats
volume.
7 Related Work
World models in language models. Probing
shows sequence models can carry structured in-
ternal state (Li et al., 2023; Nanda et al., 2023; Kim
and Schuster, 2023); audits show good prediction
can coexist with a poor model of the generating
process (Vafa et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024; Vafa
et al., 2025)—they observe; we intervene. Physics-
of-LMs (Allen-Zhu and Li, 2023) manipulates data
properties; we manipulate the objective’s answer
form, freezing the data. Supervision-content manip-
ulations exist—traces with answers fixed (Bhambri
et al., 2026), formats in logic tuning (Zhou et al.,
2025)—without byte-identical inputs or counterfac-
tual grading. Prakash et al. (2024) argue fine-tuning
enhances existing mechanisms; our base starts at
guessing, our placebo stays flat.
Limits of verifier-scored RL. Whether RLVR
expands or merely elicits capability is contested
(Yue et al., 2025; Chu et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025a;
Shao et al., 2024; DeepSeek-AI, 2025); curation
methods now assume RL needs the right SFT seed—
the premise we measure (Yao et al., 2026). We
contribute an oracle-graded controlled cell—one
verifier, one start, uses dissociated—and a positive
characterization: scores route; dense answers dom-
inate (Uesato et al., 2022; Lightman et al., 2024).
LLMs for structural engineering. Zero-shot
translator-plus-solver systems and spatial-physics
benchmarks exist (Liang et al., 2025; Siedler,
2025)—the LLM translates while a hardcoded
solver computes. Hage and Buehler (2026) RL-
tunes a compact LLM on scalar beam statics
(24 instances, uncontrolled)—consistent with our
elicitation-regime account (§4). Ours is, to our
knowledge, the first LLM trained on spatial (per-
story) structural response, and the first controlled
study of one.
8 Conclusion
The OraclePhys framework turns “what did train-
ing teach?” into a controlled variable—structural
mechanics as a model organism. The label’s answer
form determines what fine-tuning teaches; within
the recipes tested, only written or score-filtered
answers teach—advantage-weighted scores route.
Limitations
One scale, one recipe, synthetic domains. All
results are 8B + LoRA, with GRPO at ≤ 800 steps
and group sizes up to 50; full-parameter training
and prolonged-RL regimes (Liu et al., 2025a) re-
main open, and our negative claims are scoped
accordingly (§4). Both testbeds are synthetic text
over solvable physics, and heat conduction mir-
rors frames structurally: the replication evidences
recipe robustness, not domain generality.
Behavioral claims only. “Installs a forward
model” is operationalized behaviorally; linear
probes do not adjudicate here (§2.1: they decode
equally from every arm, including the behaviorally
inert O, at the surface baseline) (Hewitt and Liang,
2019). We make no mechanistic claim; probing
during generation is an open direction.
Evaluation scope. Post-edit structures belong
to a family seen in training (the out-of-format evi-
dence is the action interface). All evaluation axes
are ordinal, so magnitude-trained arms (A/K/V)
may install value models these axes do not credit—
“installs less” means “on these axes”; a value-
prediction axis (P should fail, V lead) is a natural
extension.
One template; one in-context control. Descrip-
tions instantiate a single fixed template—the price
of byte-identical control; a paraphrased evaluation
surface survives (Table 9). The frontier compar-
ison is one model, one k , text-only; many-shot
(Agarwal et al., 2024) and tool use are untested—a
tool-augmented model would likely solve the task,
but what the tool knows is not what the weights
carry.
Statistical scope. Gate arms carry three seeds;
the control-suite arms (K/V/G/S) are single runs,
to be read against the gate arms’ spread ( ± 0 . 06 );
both decisive GRPO cells carry three seeds (§4).
“Statistically indistinguishable” reports a failure to
reject except where a TOST-style bound is given
(Table 8).
Ethics Statement
OraclePhys is fully synthetic: all structures are
procedurally generated; no human subjects, anno-
tators, or personal data are involved anywhere. The
testbed and any released checkpoints are research
artifacts for studying training objectives and must
not be used for real structural design, assess-
ment, or code compliance : the FE oracle imple-
ments a simplified 2-D linear model that does not
represent engineering practice. One hazard is spe-
cific to the data release: the OraclePhys-30K S par-
tition carries deliberately shuffled (false) physics
labels—it exists as a placebo control and must
never be used as training supervision outside that
role; its datasheet flags every affected file. The
release ships under a research license with this
intended-use statement attached, alongside the li-
censes of the assets it builds on (OpenSees, Qwen3,
Llama-3.1, subject to their respective terms).

All instance streams are deterministic, so every

every number in the paper regenerates from the

stance, surface-formula reference rows recomputed
on the exported streams, and a SHA-256 over all
truths as integrity fingerprints—external models
can be scored, and paired against every model re-
ported here, without installing the FE stack.

D Alternative-explanation sweep for §4
Reward design. The reward (Appendix C) is
graded, not binary: 60% continuous full-profile
rank correlation plus 40% explicit localization
credit, with a parse floor that preserves gradient
toward well-formed answers. The two densifica-
tions a critic would propose—reward the profile
shape; reward localization directly—are both al-
ready present. What no scalar reward can add is
the label’s content itself (§4).
Optimizer health. Over GRPO training the re-
ward climbs 0 . 80 → 0 . 93 and in-pool localiza-
tion 0 . 74 → 0 . 88 while OOD localization moves
+0 . 01 : optimization succeeds at its stated objec-
tive; the objective is satisfiable without transfer-
able physics. The headroom-matched relaunch re-
produces the pattern from the lower start: reward
0 . 62 → 0 . 69 , in-pool localization 0 . 41 → 0 . 55
(first- vs. last-40-step means), OOD +0 . 013 .
Exploration. The round-2 recipe trains exclu-
sively on unsolved prompts (greedy-score filtering)
with g =8 samples at temperature 1.0; OOD lo-
calization moves 0 . 667 → 0 . 687 ( p =0 . 15 vs. the
dense control’s 0.747).
Capacity. The identical LoRA configuration
absorbs +0 . 09 to +0 . 14 on every axis when the
oracle writes answers (Table 1), so parametric ca-
pacity does not bind.
E Thinking-channel details (§5)
Direct-answer SFT leaves the model unable to use
its thinking mode: asked to reason before answer-
ing, 100% of generations hit the token limit without
closing the think block. The rationale bridge is 4k
automatically generated chains of the form “evi-
dence lines → verdict → answer”—evidence lines
read off structure features (sections, bracing, dam-
age, load shape), the verdict names the governing
story, the answer repeats the JSON ranking—fine-
tuned on top of the dense-SFT checkpoint with the
same LoRA configuration. After the bridge, think-
ing terminates in ∼ 170 tokens with zero clipping,
and length stays stable ( ∼ 172 tokens) throughout
subsequent RL, so the on/off contrast in §5 runs
on identical weights with a functioning channel in
both conditions.
